name: ERP with bookkeeping for US micro businesses
about: Building an online ERP with simple bookkeeping for US micro businesses - freelancers, sole proprietors and LLCs with 1-10 people: invoicing with online payments, expenses with bank feeds and receipt capture, a double-entry ledger, state sales tax, 1099 contractors, Schedule C categories, financial reports and basic inventory. Three stages: invoicing MVP, expenses and bookkeeping, then reports, taxes and ERP basics with the public launch. External reviews (CPA, penetration test, legal) are under opex, in USD. The top of the tree is split into stages (milestones), and every stage has the same four phases: Analysis, Implementation, Tests and Deployment, so each stage ends with something released and signed off. Every task is estimated in man-days on a T-shirt scale (XS 0.5, S 1, M 3, L 5, XL 10); parents roll up from the tasks below them.

items.name: Target users: freelancers, sole proprietors, LLCs with 1-10 people
Competitor analysis: invoicing and small-business accounting apps - features, pricing, reviews
US requirements: state sales tax, 1099-NEC, Schedule C, record keeping
Core flow: estimate to invoice to payment
Multi-tenant architecture and double-entry ledger design
Security plan: encryption, access control, SOC 2 readiness
Sign-up and company profile: EIN, address, fiscal year
Estimates and invoices with PDF and email
Online invoice payments: card and ACH
State sales tax rates through a tax API
End to end: estimate to paid invoice
Chart of accounts template mapped to Schedule C lines
Double-entry general ledger and journal entries
Bank feeds: connect accounts and import transactions
Receipt capture with OCR on mobile
Ledger integrity: debits always equal credits
M3: Reports, taxes and ERP basics
Reports: profit and loss, balance sheet, cash flow, AR and AP aging, sales tax liability
ERP scope for micro firms: inventory, purchase orders, time tracking
Sales tax liability report and filing reminders
Time tracking and billable hours to invoices
Performance with five years of data
Terms of service and privacy policy review by a lawyer
